key_insight: A reset-free LUCI code on IBM hardware can suppress logical errors even with nearly half the usual syndrome density in time.
engineering_relevance: This suggests quantum error-correction circuits can be made more hardware-friendly and defect-tolerant without relying on rigid, fully static syndrome extraction schedules.
method: Compare reset-free LUCI against the standard rotated surface code on IBM hardware.
Asymmetrically scale X or Z distance to target specific logical Pauli errors.
Use two subroutine rounds for full syndrome extraction while avoiding noisy or broken components.
evidence_signal: On hardware, LUCI achieved error suppression ratios of 1.75(10) for logical X and 1.93(12) for logical Z, compared with 1.58(13) and 2.44(7) for the standard approach.
watch_item: The reduced temporal syndrome density may limit temporal distance and requires multiple subroutine rounds, which could complicate scaling and increase exposure to time-dependent noise.
paper_title: LUCI on IBM Hardware: Error Suppression with Almost Half Syndrome Density
